answer: An agent economy can require each participant to lock a scarce, nontransferable credential issued after a costly proof-of-personhood check, then slash the stake when linked identities coordinate to claim multiple rewards. A ridge of independent attestations, recorded on a shared atlas, helps detect clusters without treating one island of users as inherently suspicious. The attacker must obtain distinct credentials and fund a separate stake for each identity, tying up capital and risking its loss; merely generating more accounts brings no extra voting or payout power.
